description: Minions, tonight we steal, the moon!
summary:
Beyond Seven Sols is a web-based interactive visual novel that brings to life the story of Sojourner, NASA’s first successful Mars rover. Despite its pioneering contributions to space exploration, Sojourner’s story often remains buried in technical documentation that can be difficult for younger audiences to access. Our project aims to bridge this gap.

Grounded in historical records and the chronology of the 1997 Mars Pathfinder mission, players gradually reconstruct Sojourner’s journey through an evolving mission report, documenting scientific discoveries and historical milestones across successive Martian sols.

Through interactive gameplay inspired by real mission procedures, players experience parachute-assisted landing, navigate challenging Martian terrain, analyze rock compositions, and perform rover wheel tests. These activities transform complex engineering and scientific concepts into hands-on learning experiences.
To bring these discoveries to life, we personify Sojourner as a curious explorer and Pathfinder as its dependable companion. Their friendship unfolds through vibrant, whimsical, storybook-inspired visuals to create an emotional connection with younger players.

By combining historical accuracy, interactive learning, and heartfelt storytelling, we hope to inspire awe, curiosity, and a lasting interest in space exploration while celebrating the enduring legacy of these forgotten pioneers.
details:
Problem and Motivation

We chose the Mars Pathfinder mission because we recognized its potential to demonstrate how the scientific legacy of a spacecraft extends far beyond its operational lifetime. Three key considerations motivated our choice.

Firstly, Mars Pathfinder marked the beginning of a new era of Martian exploration. As NASA's first successful Mars rover, Sojourner pioneered technologies and exploration methods that helped pave the way for subsequent generations of rovers, including Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Perseverance. By revisiting this mission, we hope to introduce younger audiences to the early technological breakthroughs that laid the foundation for the modern Mars rovers they may be more familiar with.

Secondly, the relationship between Sojourner and Pathfinder provides a natural foundation for emotional storytelling. The two spacecraft were designed to work together, and their technological interdependence can be translated into a meaningful friendship between two characters. For instance, Pathfinder's inability to move and Sojourner's reliance on Pathfinder for communication serve as both narrative devices and representations of the mission's real engineering constraints. Through personification, we aim to make these technical concepts more intuitive while encouraging younger players to develop an emotional connection with the spacecraft and their journey.

Lastly, their story challenges conventional perceptions of abandoned space equipment. Space missions are often celebrated for their launches, discoveries, and technological achievements, while comparatively little attention is given to the equipment left behind after their missions end. Through our interactive narrative, we encourage players to reconsider what it means for a spacecraft to be abandoned. Rather than viewing Sojourner and Pathfinder as obsolete machines, we hope players will recognize them as pioneering explorers whose scientific contributions continue to shape humanity's journey into space.

Story Structure and Narrative Choice

Our narrative combines two complementary perspectives: Sojo's emotional journey of exploration and a historically grounded account of the Mars Pathfinder mission.

We personify Sojourner and Pathfinder as two companions exploring an unfamiliar Martian world. Sojo is portrayed as a curious, enthusiastic, and determined young explorer, while Pathfinder serves as its calm, dependable companion. 

Our storyline follows the chronology of the 1997 Mars Pathfinder mission, from its arrival and Sojourner's first movements to its scientific investigations, extended operations, and eventual loss of communication. Each major narrative event is inspired by real mission objectives, scientific discoveries, or engineering challenges. For example, Sojo's encounters with Martian rocks such as Barnacle Bill and Yogi are portrayed as opportunities to make new friends, while simultaneously introducing players to the actual geological investigations conducted during the mission.

The emotional narrative is complemented by retrospective scenes that reveal the historical context and scientific significance of these events. As players progress, their discoveries are documented in an evolving mission report, gradually building a record of Sojourner's scientific achievements.

As the story unfolds, Sojo's determination to fulfill its mission and Pathfinder's unwavering support create a sense of companionship and purpose. Their journey eventually culminates in the loss of communication with Earth, marking an emotional turning point in the narrative.

However, the story does not end with their silence. Through a retrospective exploration of their legacy, players discover how the mission's scientific findings and technological innovations helped pave the way for future generations of Mars rovers.

Ultimately, we aim to transform historical spacecraft from distant technological artifacts into relatable pioneers whose journeys inspire curiosity, empathy, and appreciation for humanity's progress in space exploration.

Gameplay and Educational Mechanisms

Beyond Seven Sols combines interactive visual storytelling with mission-based gameplay inspired by the actual scientific and engineering challenges of the Mars Pathfinder mission. Players progress through different Martian sols, completing tasks that introduce scientific concepts through hands-on exploration.

Each mission features a distinct gameplay mechanic based on real mission procedures:

  • Landing: Players navigate Pathfinder's parachute-assisted descent and airbag landing, learning about spacecraft landing technologies.
  • Rover Navigation: Players guide Sojo across challenging Martian terrain, exploring autonomous navigation, obstacle avoidance, and the six-wheel rocker-bogie suspension system.
  • Approaching Rock for Chemical Analysis: Players investigate Martian rocks such as Barnacle Bill and Yogi using simplified mechanics 
  • Wheel Tests: Players perform mobility experiments to investigate wheel traction, soil properties, and rover performance on uneven terrain.

After completing each mission, players unlock narrative rewards and historical insights that connect their actions to real scientific discoveries and engineering achievements.

Throughout the journey, players also contribute to an evolving mission report, where scientific findings, historical milestones, and observations are recorded as entries from Sojo's perspective. This allows players to revisit their discoveries and gradually build a comprehensive understanding of the mission.

By integrating scientific concepts directly into gameplay, we transform passive learning into active exploration, encouraging players to understand what Sojourner discovered and how those discoveries were made.

NASA Data and Historical Accuracy

To ensure scientific and historical accuracy, we used NASA's Mars Pathfinder Mission Archive, JPL engineering documentation, and historical mission records as the foundation for our storytelling, gameplay mechanics, and visual design.

  • Historical Mission Records: Our storyline follows the chronology of the 1997 Mars Pathfinder mission, incorporating real mission objectives, scientific discoveries, and historical milestones.
  • Engineering Documentation: Sojourner's navigation systems, six-wheel rocker-bogie suspension, and wheel experiments inspired our interactive gameplay mechanics.
  • Martian Landscape Imagery: NASA's photographs and panoramic images of the Ares Vallis landing site informed our environment design, terrain layouts, and visual assets.

By integrating NASA's historical and scientific information directly into the narrative and gameplay, we aim to help players experience how discoveries were made rather than simply reading about their results.

While the characters and dialogue are fictionalized to engage younger audiences, the underlying scientific concepts and historical events remain grounded in NASA's documented mission.

Technical implementation and creative decisions

Beyond Seven Sols is developed using the following tools and technologies:

  • Next.js 16 & React 19: Core frameworks for building the interactive web game, user interface, and navigation.
  • TypeScript: Provides type safety and structures the game's logic and components.
  • XState: Manages narrative progression, game states, and scene transitions.
  • Zustand: Manages player progress, preferences, and application state.
  • GSAP: Creates cinematic animations, smooth transitions, and visual effects.
  • PixiJS & WebGL: Render atmospheric particles and interactive 2D visual effects.
  • CSS: Handles responsive layouts, interface styling, and visual design.
  • SVG, PNG & WebP: Provide game illustrations, character assets, backgrounds, and UI graphics.
  • Howler.js: Manages background music, sound effects, and audio playback.
  • Web Speech API: Provides optional text-to-speech narration using browser voices.
  • localStorage: Saves player progress and settings locally in the browser.
  • Python: Generates original audio assets and sound effects.
  • Bun: Manages dependencies and runs development and production scripts.
  • ESLint: Checks code quality and identifies potential issues.
  • React Three Fiber (Planned): Intended for future 3D rover exploration gameplay.
